This page is for *after* class, before the homework: one problem type run
twice — **fully worked**, then a **faded twin** where the middle steps are
yours, each confirmed by a gate. Ungraded; classmates encouraged.

```{=html}
<div class="fl-reveal-all"></div>
```

## Part 1 — fully worked: what the bolts feel

*A fire nozzle necks an 80 mm hose down to 30 mm, passing 20 L/s of water
to atmosphere. Find the force on the flange bolts.*

**Step 0 — the CV.** Cut at the flange, wrap the nozzle, exit at the tip.
The unknown bolt force appears as an external force on the cut — module
5.1's slice-through-the-steel move, used exactly as advertised.

**Step 1 — kinematics.** $V_1 = Q/A_1 = 3.98$ m/s;
$V_2 = Q/A_2 = 28.3$ m/s. A 7× area squeeze is a 7× speed-up —
continuity before anything else.

**Step 2 — the inlet pressure.** Bernoulli across the short, smooth
nozzle: $p_1 = \tfrac{\rho}{2}(V_2^2 - V_1^2) = 392$ kPa
gauge. *Why gauge:* atmosphere pushes on every outer surface of the CV and
on the jet; gauge nets it out in one stroke.

**Step 3 — momentum.** $x$-balance on the CV:
$p_1A_1 - F_{bolts} = \dot m (V_2 - V_1)$, so
$$F = p_1 A_1 - \rho Q (V_2 - V_1)
= 1969 - 485 = 1483\ \text{N (tension)}.$$
The pressure term *wants* to blow the nozzle off; the momentum change
refunds part of it. The bolts hold the difference — about
151 kg-force of steady pull.

## Part 2 — the faded twin: the smaller rig

*A 65 mm hose, 25 mm tip, 12 L/s. Same CV, same three purchases.*


::: {#u5w-s3 .fl-hidden}
```{=html}
<div class="fl-checkpoint"
     data-prompt="Step 3 — bolt force = p₁A₁ − ρQ(V₂ − V₁)?"
     data-answer="719" data-tol="0.03" data-units="N"
     data-hint="Two terms, opposite corners: pressure-area pushes the nozzle off; momentum flux buys some back. If you got ~970 N you kept only the pressure term."
     data-solution="F = 968 − 250 = 719 N of tension."
     data-target="u5w-s4"></div>
```
:::

::: {#u5w-s4 .fl-hidden}
**What transferred.** Continuity → Bernoulli → momentum, and the sign
discipline: pressure-area terms and momentum-flux terms sit on opposite
sides of the ledger, and the hardware carries the *difference*. Skip the
momentum refund and you overdesign every flange you touch by a third.
:::

## Let the toolbox referee

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
import numpy as np
for label, D1, D2, Q in [("Part 1", 0.080, 0.030, 0.020), ("Part 2", 0.065, 0.025, 0.012)]:
    A1, A2 = np.pi/4*D1**2, np.pi/4*D2**2
    V1, V2 = Q/A1, Q/A2
    p1 = 998.2/2*(V2**2 - V1**2)
    F = p1*A1 - 998.2*Q*(V2 - V1)
    print(f"{label}: V2 = {V2:.1f} m/s, p1 = {p1/1000:.0f} kPa gauge, bolt force = {F:.0f} N")
```
